editorial:
If you love a good serial killer mystery with a creepy edge, Longlegs is going to pull you in fast. The story follows FBI Agent Lee Harker, a sharp new recruit who gets thrown into a cold case about a killer who leaves strange clues behind. As she digs deeper, things get weird in the best way, with hints of the occult and a personal link to the killer that hits close to home. The vibe is dark, tense, and full of slow-burn dread that keeps you guessing.

The acting is strong, especially the lead, who makes you feel every bit of her fear and determination. The pacing is steady, building tension without rushing, though some viewers might find the middle a bit slow. The visuals are moody and the sound design adds real chills. If you enjoy crime thrillers with a supernatural twist, this one is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you learn that Harker's mother was secretly helping Longlegs all along, using dark rituals to protect her daughter. The killer was never working alone. Harker confronts her mother and Longlegs in a tense showdown, and she is forced to make a heartbreaking choice to stop the cycle. The movie ends with Harker surviving but forever changed, carrying the weight of her family's dark secret.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves crime thrillers with a supernatural twist
